records.name: Tabita
records.facts_used: Tabita: Tabita is linked to Aramaic Ṭabīthā, gazelle. In the New Testament tradition the name also has the Greek equivalent Dorcas. The animal word is its lexical base, rather than a Latvian compound inferred from similar sounds. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Tabita: 1923, Riga. Its calendar year is 1934. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p301 ownRiga1923/calendar 1934. Biblical narrative is identified as textual tradition, not independent proof of a miraculous event.

records.name: Zenons
records.facts_used: Zenons: The family’s Greek base is Zēnōn, connected with Zēnos, a form of the name Zeus. It refers to a Greek deity’s name rather than a separate full sentence. The ancient root does not itself determine a modern bearer’s religion or character. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Zenons: 1877, Rēzekne. Its calendar year is 1864. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.

records.name: Zenobija
records.facts_used: Zenobija: The documented Zenobia family combines Greek Zēnos, of Zeus, and bios, life. It is a two-element name referring to Zeus, distinct from a simple Zēnōn derivative. The exact Latvian spelling is established by a rendering record. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Zenobia → Zenobija, citing page 121 of a 2006 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact English feminine given-name row2006p121. Pronunciation annotation[-ō-] not another spelling. Zinobija/Zinovija dates not transferred.

records.name: Gedenė
records.facts_used: Gedenė: The guide links Gedenė with Geda/Gedė and longer Ged- names such as Gedmina and Gedvilė. The common element is compared with Lithuanian gedėti, to mourn. These full forms need not be collapsed into one obligatory base name or an invented full-name translation. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Gedenė (Geda) on 9 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
